The problem with a system like that is that in a lot of games defeating enemies is the primary way in which you gain experience and accumulate resources, which means that if enemies run away from you the player has to chase them if they don't want to miss out on the experience and loot. That shifts the tone of the game completely, you're no longer fighting enemies, you're hunting them.

The only way to have a game where intimidating enemies into not fighting you, avoiding them through stealth etc. are actually good tactics are games where you don't level up with the number of enemies you defeat but the number of objectives you complete. For example, in Vampire The Masquerade: Bloodlines, enemies will sometimes start running away from you if you terrify them using vampiric powers, or rip apart a few of their friends. You can also complete the whole game through stealth and avoid killing enemies. But the game gets away with all that because it only gives you XP for completing objectives, never for how many enemies you've killed.
